newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--FBI officials will join the Greek anti-terrorist police in their investigation of Wednesday's murder by the notorious November 17 group of Greek shipowner Constantine Peratikos. There is an absence of strong leads in the investigation with the only new element being the discovery that the perpertrators also used a .38 calibre gun.

--The Bank of Greece did battle for the third consecutive day to keep the drachma up to par with the Ecu as 800 million dollars left the country. The bank said it had taken all the measures necessary to neutralise the pressure on the drachma.

--Greece's elusive terrorists, November 17, claimed responsibility for the murder of Peratikos on Wednesday with an eight-page declaration published today. November 17 reveals that it tried to kill Peratikos on at least two other occasions and calls the sale of the Elefsis Shipyards to the Peratikos family in 1992 "a great scandal".

--Increasing the tax-free threshold for wage-earners and pensioners and possibly others is being examined by the finance ministry as are changes to tax declaration forms and the indexation of the tax scale.

--"Whoever searches, finds," Maria Bossi, the public order ministry's former expert on organised crime says. "There are no secret organisations in Greece, no ghosts.. (November 17) is not a leftist organisation - it uses democratic symbols to mask criminal acts".
--Greek shipowners have put up 2.7 billion drachmas as a reward for information on the November 17 murder of one of their numbers, Costas Peratikos, reports say.

--Television personality Nikos Mastorakis has filed suit against Olympic Airways for forcing him to fly with non-Olympic aircraft and foreign cabin crews due to problems with Olympic cabin crews and scheduling.
--Deputy Finance Minister George Drys says Greeks will receive 300,000 drachmas if they trade in their old technology cars for new.
--The problem of November 17's terrorism could have been solved if the state was really interested, Bossi says. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
